He has previously played for the [[San Antonio Spurs]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) and with the [[Austin Spurs]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence Friars]]. ==Early life== Duke was born and raised in [[Providence, Rhode Island]].{{cite news |title=Providence roots unite rivals |url=https://www.nbl.com.au/news/duke-jr-credits-perth-teammates-in-battle-of-friars |access-date=November 10, 2025 |work=nbl.com.au |date=November 10, 2025 |language=en}} He grew up playing [[association football|soccer]] and [[American football|football]] and running [[track and field|track]], not fully devoting himself to basketball until high school.{{cite web |last=Casey |first=Tim |title=Providence College Guard David Duke Excelling For Hometown Team |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/timcasey/2020/03/12/providence-college-guard-david-duke-excelling-for-hometown-team/ |website=[[Forbes]] |access-date=November 3, 2020 |date=March 12, 2020}} ==High school career== As a freshman at [[Classical High School]] in Providence, Duke stood {{convert|5|ft|6|in}} and played at the [[junior varsity team|junior varsity]] level. Duke grew to {{convert|6|ft|1|in}} and joined the [[varsity team]] in his sophomore season. As a junior, he averaged 15 points per game and led his team to a Division 1 state title.{{cite web |last=Cordova |first=David |title=David Duke: A Local Talent Stars As A Freshman For Providence |url=https://davesjoint.net/2018/11/25/david-duke-a-local-talent-stars-as-a-freshman-for-providence/ |website=Dave's Joint |access-date=November 3, 2020 |date=November 25, 2018}} After the season, Duke transferred to [[Cushing Academy]] in [[Ashburnham, Massachusetts]] and repeated his junior year due to [[reclassification (education)|reclassification]]. He played with [[Wabissa Bede]] and helped his team win the [[New England Preparatory School Athletic Council]] (NEPSAC) Class AA title.{{cite web |last=Farrahar |first=Kevin |title=David Duke's Time is Here |url=http://friarbasketball.com/2018/11/06/david-dukes-time/ |website=Friar Basketball |access-date=November 3, 2020 |date=November 6, 2018}} As a senior, Duke averaged 17 points, five rebounds and four assists per game and helped Cushing reach the NEPSAC Class AA semifinals. A four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence]] over offers from [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]], [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]], [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] and [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]].{{cite web |last=McNamara |first=Kevin |title=David Duke to stay home, picks Providence College |url=https://www.providencejournal.com/sports/20171013/david-duke-to-stay-home-picks-providence-college |website=[[The Providence Journal]] |access-date=November 3, 2020 |date=October 13, 2017}} ==College career== Entering his first season at Providence, Duke shared preseason [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Big East Freshman of the Year]] honors with [[Jahvon Quinerly]].{{cite web |last=McNamara |first=Kevin |title=PC's David Duke named preseason co-Freshman of the Year in Big East |url=https://www.providencejournal.com/sports/20181025/pcs-david-duke-named-preseason-co-freshman-of-year-in-big-east |website=[[The Providence Journal]] |access-date=November 3, 2020 |date=October 15, 2018}} He immediately became the team's starting point guard but moved off the ball by the end of the season.{{cite web |last=Farrahar |first=Kevin |title=What's in Store for David Duke in Year 2? |url=http://friarbasketball.com/2019/09/30/whats-store-david-duke-year-2/ |website=Friar Basketball |access-date=November 3, 2020 |date=September 30, 2019}} On November 17, 2018, Duke scored a freshman season-high 20 points in a 76–67 win over [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]].{{cite web |title=Duke & Diallo Lead PC Past South Carolina 76–67, Face #18 Michigan Sunday |url=https://www.golocalprov.com/sports/new-pc-falls-to-south-carolina |website=GoLocalProv |access-date=November 3, 2020 |date=November 18, 2018}} As a freshman, he averaged 7.1 points, 2.6 rebounds and 2.1 assists per game.{{cite web |last=Mallard |first=Nick |title=Former Cushing Academy stars still shining in college postseason |url=https://www.sentinelandenterprise.com/2019/03/19/former-cushing-academy-stars-still-shining-in-college-postseason/ |website=[[Sentinel & Enterprise]] |access-date=November 3, 2020 |date=March 19, 2019}} On January 18, 2020, Duke scored a sophomore season-high 36 points, shooting 6-of-8 from three-point range, in a 78–74 loss to [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]].{{cite web |title=Despite 36 Points from Duke, PC Falls to #25 Creighton 78–74 |url=https://www.golocalprov.com/sports/new-despite-36-points-from-duke-pc-falls-to-25-creighton-78-74 |website=GoLocalProv |access-date=November 3, 2020 |date=January 18, 2020}}{{cite web |last=Steele |first=Ian |title=One-on-One with PC's David Duke after Career-High 36 Point Performance |url=https://www.abc6.com/oneonone-with-pcs-david-duke-after-careerhigh-36-point-performance/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210911035425/https://www.abc6.com/oneonone-with-pcs-david-duke-after-careerhigh-36-point-performance/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 11, 2021 |website=[[WLNE-TV]] |access-date=November 3, 2020 |date=January 21, 2020}} As a sophomore, he averaged 12 points, 4.2 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 1.5 steals per game, shooting 42 percent on three-pointers.{{cite web |last=Foley |first=Brian |title=Providence Basketball: Friars' David Duke poised as Big East's breakout star Duke averaged 16.8 points, 6.3 rebounds and 4.8 assists per game as a junior.{{cite news |last=Koch |first=Bill |title=Ex-Friar David Duke invited to NBA Combine |url=https://www.providencejournal.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2021/06/15/former-providence-college-friars-guard-david-duke-has-been-invited-nba-combine/7708860002/ |access-date=June 22, 2021 |work=[[The Providence Journal]] |date=June 15, 2021}} He was named to the Second Team [[List of All-Big East Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big East]].{{cite news |last=Steele |first=Ian |title=David Duke, Nate Watson Named Second Team All BIG EAST |url=https://www.abc6.com/david-duke-nate-watson-named-second-team-all-big-east/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210308023145/https://www.abc6.com/david-duke-nate-watson-named-second-team-all-big-east/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 8, 2021 |access-date=June 22, 2021 |work=ABC6 |date=March 7, 2021}} On April 2, 2021, Duke declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility. ==Professional career== ===Brooklyn Nets / Long Island Nets (2021–2023)=== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Duke signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]] on August 8, 2021.{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign David Duke Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2021/08/08/brooklyn-nets-sign-david-duke-jr|website=NBA.com|date=August 8, 2021|access-date=September 2, 2021}} He played for the Nets during the [[2021 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web |title=David Duke Player Profile, Phoenix Suns – RealGM |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/David-Duke/Summary/119514 |website=basketball.realgm.com |access-date=October 24, 2025 |language=en}} On October 16, the Nets converted Duke to a [[two-way contract]].{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Exercise Two-Way Player Conversion on David Duke Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2021/10/16/brooklyn-nets-exercise-two-way-player-conversion-on-david-duke-jr|website=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2021|access-date=October 17, 2021}} He subsequently split his time during the [[2021–22 Brooklyn Nets season|2021–22 season]] between Brooklyn and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Long Island Nets]]. Duke joined the Nets for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]] after turning down a new two-way contract offer from the team.{{cite web|first=Brian|last=Lewis|title=David Duke Jr. eyeing standard Nets contract after rejecting two-way offer|url=https://nypost.com/2022/07/09/david-duke-jr-eyeing-standard-nets-contract-after-two-way-offer/|website=NYPost.com|date=July 9, 2022|access-date=February 22, 2023}} However, he ultimately re-signed with the Nets on a two-way deal on September 16, 2022,{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Re-sign David Duke Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-re-sign-david-duke-jr|website=NBA.com|date=September 16, 2022|access-date=February 22, 2023}} once again splitting the [[2022–23 Brooklyn Nets season|2022–23 season]] between Brooklyn and Long Island. Duke was named to the G League's inaugural Next Up Game in February 2023.{{cite web|title=Wolves' Garza And Ignite's Henderson Named Captains For NBA G League Next Up Game|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/wolves-garza-and-ignites-henderson-named-captains-for-nba-g-league-next-up-game|website=NBA.com|date=February 7, 2023|access-date=March 8, 2023}} In 22 games with Long Island during the [[2022–23 NBA G League season]], Duke averaged a team-leading 22.9 points (fifth in the NBA G League) on 47.8 percent shooting from the field, 32.1 percent shooting from 3-point range and 80.5 percent shooting from the free-throw line, to go with 6.1 rebounds, 3.8 assists and 1.9 steals (10th in the NBA G League) in a team-high 34.2 minutes per game. He also appeared in seven NBA G League Showcase games and played in two postseason games for Long Island, averaging 21.6 and 16.0 points per game, respectively.{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Convert David Duke Jr. Contract to Standard NBA Deal|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-convert-david-duke-jr-contract-to-standard-nba-deal|website=NBA.com|date=April 7, 2023|access-date=April 7, 2023}} He finished third in the [[NBA G League Most Valuable Player Award]] voting and was named to the [[All-NBA G League Team|All-NBA G League First Team]].{{cite news |title=Windy City Bulls' Carlik Jones Headlines 2022–23 All-NBA G League Teams |url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/windy-city-bulls-carlik-jones-headlines-2022-23-all-nba-g-league-teams |access-date=October 24, 2025 |work=The NBA G League |date=April 14, 2023 |language=en}} On April 7, 2023, Duke signed a standard contract with Brooklyn to finish the season. He then re-joined the Nets for the [[2023 NBA Summer League]]. ===Delaware Blue Coats (2023)=== On September 11, 2023, Duke signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]],{{cite web|title=David Duke Jr. Signs With 76ers|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-sign-david-duke-jr|website=NBA.com|date=September 11, 2023|access-date=September 12, 2023}} but was waived on October 20.{{cite web |last=Maher |first=Rory |date=October 20, 2023 |title=Sixers Waive Ricky Council, David Duke Jr. |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/10/sixers-waive-ricky-council-david-duke-jr.html |access-date=October 25, 2023 |website=HoopsRumors.com}} He subsequently joined the [[Delaware Blue Coats]] for the [[2023–24 NBA G League season]].{{cite tweet|author=Delaware Blue Coats|title=time for camp.🏕️ #GetYourCoatsOn|number=1718729617358418138|user=blue_coats|date=October 29, 2023|access-date=November 10, 2023}} In 11 games with the Blue Coats, he averaged 21.7 points, 5.5 rebounds, 4.1 assists in 31.5 minutes.{{cite web|first=Alex|last=Garcia|title=Spurs Sign David Duke Jr. to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-sign-david-duke-jr-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=December 14, 2023|access-date=December 14, 2023}} ===San Antonio / Austin Spurs (2023–2025)=== On December 14, 2023, Duke signed a two-way contract with the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. In 38 games (37 starts) with the [[Austin Spurs]] during the 2023–24 NBA G League season, he averaged a team-high 19.8 points to go with 6.4 rebounds, 4.6 assists and 1.3 steals in 32.9 minutes per game.{{cite web |last=Shirley|first=P. |title=Spurs Sign David Duke Jr. to a Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-sign-david-duke-jr-to-a-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 26, 2024|access-date=July 26, 2024}} He then finished the [[2023–24 San Antonio Spurs season|2023–24 NBA season]] averaging 6.5 points, 2.5 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 12.8 minutes in four games for San Antonio. Despite being sidelined for the [[2024 NBA Summer League]],{{cite news |last1=Douglas |first1=Jacob |title=Spurs sign David Duke Jr. to a two-way contract |url=https://www.poundingtherock.com/2024/7/26/24207098/san-antonio-spurs-sign-david-duke-jr-to-a-two-way-contract-dominick-barlow-victor-wembanyama |access-date=October 24, 2025 |work=Pounding The Rock |date=July 26, 2024}} Duke re-signed with San Antonio on another two-way contract on July 26, 2024. He appeared in six games with San Antonio during the [[2024–25 San Antonio Spurs season|2024–25 season]] while also playing with the Austin Spurs of the NBA G League, averaging 16.9 points, 6.7 rebounds and 3.1 assists in 27 regular season games (all starts).{{cite news |title=PHOENIX SUNS ANNOUNCE TRAINING CAMP ROSTER {{!}} Phoenix Suns |url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/phoenix-suns-announce-training-camp-roster |access-date=October 24, 2025 |work=suns.com |date=September 23, 2025 |language=en}} On September 23, 2025, Duke signed
